crime: Each evening, after the others went in, one girl lay on her back in the dark courtyard, phone held over her face, answering everyone's messages. Only she ever answered {WITCH_NAME}'s.
From the upper railing, {WITCH_NAME} used her Magic to draw the girl's face close as she read, to see what her words did to it.
One night the reply came: "I can see you up there. No more messages. Come down and say it to my face."
{WITCH_NAME} came down and stood over her, unable to speak. The girl laughed softly up at her. "It's only me."

A classmate had once read {WITCH_NAME}'s notes and smiled at her across the room. But when {WITCH_NAME} spoke to her face, the classmate laughed with the class and pulled her own desk away. Her words, {WITCH_NAME} learned, reached people only from far away.
{WITCH_NAME} knelt over the girl, shrank her face to a faint, far-off speck, and closed both hands on her throat until the speck stopped moving.

Another prisoner joined {WITCH_NAME} at the railing and messaged the girl: "Lockup in ten minutes. Come in." {WITCH_NAME} drew the girl close and read it off her phone word for word. The prisoner confirmed it. "She's reading it now," {WITCH_NAME} said.
The prisoner went down and found the girl dead in the grass.
In the trial court, the prisoners ruled the girl was killed after she read that message, which placed {WITCH_NAME} at the railing beside the prisoner who went down.
A prisoner noted that {WITCH_NAME}'s Magic brought things nearer but never showed their other side. A phone held over a face shows the railing only its back.
The prisoners understood: the screen {WITCH_NAME} read had lain face up on a still chest. The girl was dead before the message came, and {WITCH_NAME} had already been down.
fields.epitaph: Close enough to touch her, and still too far away to speak.
fields.epithet: The Girl Who Loved from the Railing
execution: The execution stand raises an iron board, and she is chained upright against it, a folded iron note in her hand. Before her runs a long iron rail, with a small iron face at its far end.
The face glides along the rail. It grows until it fills her sight, its mouth open in a laugh, until it meets her face and keeps pressing.
She lets the folded iron note fall, unopened, beneath the face.
The iron face rests against hers. Behind it, she hangs still.

magic.name: Near and Far
magic.text: She can make anyone or anything she sees or hears seem right in front of her, or a faint, faraway speck.
